title: Re-Depreciating a Carpet Replacement Charge on a Security Deposit Account
content:
When the carpet replacement charge on a Security Deposit Account final account statement is corrected, the carpet credit is the carpet charged less the corrected carpet charge.

## Definitions

- **Carpet charged.** The amount of the carpet replacement line itemized on the account.
- **Carpet cost basis.** The replacement cost recorded on the carpet line.
- **Carpet life.** The program's carpet useful life, in months, from the useful-life table.
- **Remaining share.** The carpet life less the carpet's age in months recorded on the line, never below 0, divided by the carpet life.
- **Corrected carpet charge.** The carpet cost basis times the remaining share, rounded half up to the cent.
- **Carpet credit.** The carpet charged less the corrected carpet charge, rounded half up to the cent.

**Records read.** The carpet replacement line's amount, replacement cost and recorded age, from the account's itemized move-out lines. The deposit program of the account.

## Worked example (hypothetical carpet, 60-month life)

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Carpet charged | 900.00 USD |
| Replacement cost recorded on the line | 1200.00 USD |
| Recorded age | 24 months |
| Remaining share: 60 less 24 is 36, divided by 60 | 0.6 |
| Corrected carpet charge: 1200.00 times 0.6 | 720.00 USD |
| Carpet credit: 900.00 less 720.00 | 180.00 USD |

## Second example (hypothetical, carpet past its life)

Recorded age 70 months on a 60-month life: 60 less 70 is below 0, so the remaining share is 0. The corrected carpet charge is 0.00. The carpet credit equals the whole amount charged for the carpet.

## Rounding example (hypothetical)

Replacement cost 1000.00 USD, age 17 months, 60-month life. The remaining share is 43 divided by 60, which is 0.71666... The corrected carpet charge is 716.666..., which rounds half up to 716.67 USD.
